title: Functional universality of critical SK autocorrelations

issues.location: Sec 2 Lemma edge-biased-law (02-edge-law.tex) and Secs 3-5 (cap/variance estimates)
issues.description: The key quantitative inputs depend on the companion manuscripts CS and CM (CS Prop 3.1, CM Prop 16.1 and Sec 15). These are the uncapped second moment E_U L_circ^2 = 1+o(1), the cap-extension construction, and the coarse curvature tolerances. The sharp conditional-variance bound (eq. source-16, order p^{-2} with no power loss) rests on them, and it could not be checked here. I sanity-checked the second-moment claim heuristically: the binomial-to-sphere overlap density ratio is exp(n rho^4/6), which goes to 1 on the n^{-1/3} overlap scale. That is consistent, but it is not a verification.
issues.evidence: "the uncapped zero-field calculation in the proof of the static cap comparison of \cite{CM}, Section~15 ... gives E_U Z_cube^2/(Z_sp)^2=1+o(1)"

main_claim: Consider the zero-field SK model at beta=1 with rate-one heat-bath dynamics. The rescaled stationary autocorrelation A_n(s) = n^{1/3} C_n(s n^{2/3}) converges in law in C_loc((0,inf)) to the same law Q_crit for both Gaussian and Rademacher couplings. Q_crit is the law of sum_a <x_a, exp(-s c_* H_Pi) x_a>_Pi for the GOE-edge-conditioned Gaussian measure Pi, with a deterministic c_* = omega({0}) > 0. It is not a point mass, and its functions are a.s. nonzero, nonnegative, nonincreasing and decay to 0.
